entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
John III of the Palatinate was the 48th Archbishop of Regensburg, reigning from 1507 until his death on February 13, 1538. A member of the powerful Palatine family, he played a crucial role in the Protestant Reformation in the Holy Roman Empire, supporting Martin Luther and participating in the Diet of Augsburg in 1530.

Born into a prominent noble family, John III's early life was marked by his education and training for the priesthood, preparing him for his eventual appointment as Archbishop. His leadership during the tumultuous period of the Reformation had significant consequences, shaping the course of religious and political events in the region.

John III's legacy extends beyond his tenure as Archbishop, as he left a lasting impact on the development of Protestantism in the Holy Roman Empire. His support for Luther and his participation in the Diet of Augsburg helped to cement the Protestant stance in the region, paving the way for future generations of reformers.

Despite his significant contributions to the Reformation, John III's life was not without controversy. His involvement in the tumultuous politics of the Holy Roman Empire led to conflicts with other powerful figures, ultimately contributing to his own downfall.

The Palatine family's influence extended far beyond John III's lifetime, with his descendants playing a significant role in shaping European politics and religion in the centuries that followed. This legacy serves as a testament to the enduring impact of John III's life and reign.
